system_overview: This specification models a Single Producer, Multi Consumer (SPMC) Disruptor, a high-performance inter-thread communication pattern based on the LMAX Exchange Disruptor. A single producer thread publishes events into a fixed-size ring buffer, and multiple consumer threads each independently read all published events in multicast fashion. The model verifies the absence of data races between the producer and consumers and ensures all consumers eventually read all published values.
actors_and_components: The system consists of two types of participants: a single writer (producer thread) and multiple readers (consumer threads). The writer publishes events sequentially into a ring buffer. Each reader independently consumes all events from the ring buffer. The ring buffer is a shared circular data structure that tracks slot contents and which threads are actively accessing each slot.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the ring buffer contents, including the value in each slot, which readers are currently accessing each slot, and which writers are currently accessing each slot; (2) a write cursor indicating the sequence number of the last published event; (3) a read cursor per consumer indicating the last sequence number consumed by that consumer; (4) a program counter per thread indicating whether it is currently accessing a slot or advancing to the next; (5) a history variable per consumer recording the sequence of all values read, used for liveness verification.
initial_state: All ring buffer slots contain a null value with no active readers or writers. The write cursor starts at negative one (nothing published). All read cursors start at negative one (nothing consumed). All threads start in the advancing state. All consumer read histories are empty.
actions: The system has four transitions: (1) Begin write: the producer checks that the slowest consumer is far enough ahead that writing the next slot will not overwrite unconsumed data (the consumer must be at most one ring buffer cycle behind); the producer then writes its sequence number as the value into the corresponding slot, marks itself as accessing that slot, and transitions to the accessing state. (2) End write: the producer finishes writing by removing itself from the slot's writer set, advancing the write cursor to make the event visible to consumers, and transitioning back to the advancing state. (3) Begin read: a consumer checks whether the next sequence it needs to read has been published (the write cursor is at or past that sequence); if so, it marks itself as accessing the slot, records the value into its read history, and transitions to the accessing state. (4) End read: a consumer finishes reading by removing itself from the slot's reader set, advancing its read cursor, and transitioning back to the advancing state.
safety_properties: Two invariants must hold: (1) Type correctness: all variables remain within their expected domains. (2) No data races: for every slot in the ring buffer, a slot is never simultaneously being read and written (the reader and writer sets for each slot cannot both be non-empty), and at most one writer accesses any slot at a time.
liveness_properties: Eventually and permanently, every consumer must have read all published values in order. For each consumer and each sequence number up to the maximum, once the write cursor has reached or passed that sequence, the consumer will eventually have read it and recorded the correct value.
model_bounds: The maximum number of published events bounds the model. The ring buffer has a fixed size. The writer and reader sets are finite constants. A state constraint limits exploration to states where the write cursor has not reached the maximum.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for consumer read actions (both beginning and ending reads), ensuring consumers make progress when enabled. No fairness is assumed for the producer. Because there is only a single producer, the publication mechanism is simpler than the multi-producer case: the write cursor directly indicates which sequence numbers are available for reading, without needing an additional per-slot publication tracking mechanism.
